questions.question: Four AI applications each need to reach six external systems. How many implementations does one shared protocol require?
options: Six, because only the external systems implement anything at all
Four, because only the AI applications implement anything at all
Ten, because each application and each system implements it once
Twenty-four, because each pair still needs its own custom glue
questions.explanation: A shared protocol turns N times M pairings into N plus M implementations: four clients plus six servers is ten.

questions.question: In the 2026-07-28 revision, how does a server learn which protocol version a request uses?
options: From the version the server advertised in its latest tools/list reply
From the initialize handshake that opened the connection earlier on
From a session identifier the server assigned on the first request
From io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion in the request's _meta
questions.explanation: The protocol is stateless: every request carries its own protocol version and client capabilities in params._meta, with no handshake or session.

questions.question: A client sends tools/call naming a tool the server does not expose. What does a conformant server return?
options: A JSON-RPC error with code -32602 because the params are invalid
An input_required result asking the user to pick a different tool
A JSON-RPC error with code -32601 because the method is unknown
A normal result with isError set to true and an empty content list
questions.explanation: An unknown tool is a protocol error reported as -32602 Invalid params; -32601 is reserved for an unknown JSON-RPC method.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes who controls each server primitive?
options: All three primitives are chosen by the server operator ahead of time
Tools are model-controlled, resources app-driven, prompts user-controlled
Tools are user-controlled, resources model-controlled, prompts app-driven
All three primitives are chosen by the model at runtime without the host
questions.explanation: The model decides when to invoke tools, the host application decides which resources enter context, and the user explicitly selects prompts.

questions.question: A call to get_forecast omits its required city argument. Which response best helps the model recover?
options: An empty successful result so that the conversation keeps going
A JSON-RPC error -32603 that reports an internal server failure
A result with isError true that explains the city is required
A JSON-RPC error -32602 that the host withholds from the model
questions.explanation: Input problems are tool execution errors: a normal result with isError true lets the model read the explanation and retry with a city.

questions.question: Which of these does MCP deliberately leave to the host application instead of standardizing?
options: How a server describes the tools it offers to connecting clients
How a client invokes a tool and then reads the result that returns
How results and errors are shaped when they travel on the wire
Which model the host uses and how it assembles its model prompt
questions.explanation: MCP standardizes the conversation between applications and systems; the choice of model and prompt construction remain the host's decisions.
